title: Phase separation, morphology, and metastability in the three-dimensional active Potts model
abstract: We study the three-dimensional active Potts model (APM) on a cubic lattice with 2, 4, and 6 orientational states. The steady-state phase diagrams exhibit low-density gaseous, high-density polar liquid, and liquid--gas coexistence phases, with the phase behavior controlled by density, temperature, and propulsion speed and retaining the main features of the previously studied two-dimensional APM. At weak propulsion, the dense phase forms a slab perpendicular to its direction of motion. With increasing propulsion speed, this morphology persists for the 2-state model, whereas the dense phases for 4 and 6 states reorient and propagate along their longitudinal direction. For the 6-state model, the reoriented dense phase further develops a cylindrical morphology. We also examine the stability of polar liquids against artificially introduced droplets using microscopic simulations and coarse-grained hydrodynamic equations. At high propulsion speeds, counter-propagating droplets can partially modify the initial polar state, while transverse droplets can completely alter it, demonstrating the metastable nature of polar liquids in the three-dimensional active Potts model.
summary: This paper analyzes the phase behavior of the 3D active Potts model, a system modeling interacting particles with internal states and self-propulsion. Using Monte Carlo simulations and hydrodynamic theory, the authors map out phase diagrams and show how the dense phase morphology evolves from slabs to rods depending on propulsion speed. Crucially, they demonstrate that the ordered liquid phase is metastable, easily disrupted by external perturbations.
main_problem: The study investigates phase separation, morphology, and metastability in the three-dimensional active Potts model (APM).
main_result: The 3D APM exhibits distinct phase behaviors (gaseous, liquid, coexistence) whose morphology (slab vs. cylindrical) changes with propulsion speed, and the polar liquid phase is shown to be metastable against droplet perturbations.
method: The research employs Monte Carlo simulations and derives hydrodynamic equations by expanding the master equation in the continuum limit.
model_or_system: The system is the three-dimensional active Potts model (APM) on a cubic lattice with $q=2, 4,$ or $6$ orientational states. Dynamics are governed by spin-flipping rates and particle hopping rates biased by self-propulsion.
key_observables: Steady-state phase diagrams, density profiles ($ ar{ho}(x)$), and the morphology of the dense phase (slab, rod, cylinder).
important_parameters: Number of states ($q$), temperature ($ eta$), average density ($ho$), and self-propulsion bias ($\epsilon$).
main_assumptions: The analysis extends known 2D results to 3D and utilizes hydrodynamic approximations for the density evolution.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematics of hopping rates, density profiles showing phase separation, and time evolution snapshots demonstrating morphology changes (slab to rod) and the effect of droplet excitations.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the model dynamics and then analyzes the phase behavior across different $q$ values. It progresses from steady-state phase diagrams to detailed analyses of morphology changes with propulsion bias, culminating in stability tests using artificial droplet perturbations.
why_interesting: The study of active matter models like the APM provides insights into non-equilibrium phase transitions and pattern formation, which are crucial topics in modern statistical mechanics and complex systems.
